answer_1.quote: We use a human-in-the-loop pipeline that combines LLM and expert input to generate stories and multiple-choice questions.
answer_1.outputs: The paper generates legal stories and multiple-choice questions to explain and assess understanding of legal concepts.

answer_2.quote: We report the following common complexity metrics for comparison: (1) Legal Vocabulary List (LVL) occurrences, (2) Top 1000 most common words (Top1K), (3) Function words, (4) Sentence length, (5) Language model perplexity, (6) Flesch-Kincaid grade level.

answer_4.quote: We recruit human subjects with law education backgrounds on Prolific to evaluate the legal concepts and their corresponding stories generated by LLMs.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators judge the Readability of Definition (RoD) and the following metrics for the generated stories: (1) Readability of Story (RoS), (2) Relevance, (3) Redundancy, (4) Cohesiveness, (5) Completeness, (6) Factuality, (7) Likeability, (8) Believability. For questions, they judge whether the question contains specific shortcomings and rate each question from 1 (bad) to 5 (good).
